speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a generalized nonpruritic rash and a recent history of high fever and a seizure. To understand the severity and cause, have you noticed any specific features on your skin, such as bleeding spots or a "sandpaper" texture?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Measles (Rubeola). The classic triad of high fever, generalized maculopapular rash spreading from trunk to extremities, and a seizure (likely febrile) in an infant, combined with the description of a nonpruritic rash, strongly supports this diagnosis despite up-to-date immunizations. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray to assess for any complications like pneumonia.
